translationRepairs: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qiandao (1166) and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.
He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Qiandao (1166) and was appointed county defender (wei) of Yanguan.
授鹽官尉 appoints him county defender (尉) of Yanguan (鹽官); 鹽官 is the place-name, not a salt office.
In the second year of Qiandao he became a jinshi and was appointed salt commissioner of Yanguan.
In the second year of Qiandao he became a jinshi and was appointed county defender (wei) of Yanguan.
The literal repeats the same error: 尉 is the county defender, not a salt commissioner.

When his wife's parent died he left office for mourning. After mourning he served as a staff officer on the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was briefly transferred to Huaidong, then returned to Jiangdong and was appointed magistrate of Xi'an County.

When his father died he left office for mourning. After mourning he served as a staff officer on the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was briefly transferred to Huaidong, then returned to Jiangdong and was appointed magistrate of Xi'an County.
遭外艱, after earlier 丁母憂, is mourning for his father; it does not mean a parent-in-law.

He encountered mourning for a parent-in-law; when the mourning ended he served as staff officer of the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was moved to Huaidong, then returned to his former post, and was changed to magistrate of Xi'an County.

He encountered mourning for his father; when the mourning ended he served as staff officer of the Jiangdong Intendant Commission, was moved to Huaidong, then returned to his former post, and was changed to magistrate of Xi'an County.
外艱 denotes paternal mourning, not mourning for a parent-in-law.
The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him to join his staff as a counselor, but he declined and was instead appointed a staff officer in the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuoyou invited him to join his staff as a counselor, but he declined and was instead appointed a staff officer in the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
袁說友 is Yuan Shuoyou; Shuiyou misreads 說.
The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuiyou invited him into his staff as counselor, but he did not accept and was changed to staff officer of the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
The Sichuan commander Yuan Shuoyou invited him into his staff as counselor, but he did not accept and was changed to staff officer of the Bureau for Auditing Various Offices.
The literal likewise misreads 說友 as Shuiyou instead of Shuoyou.
The crown prince obtained a copy of Lou Ji's "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased with it. He ordered Dai Xi to write a colophon.
The crown prince obtained a copy of Lou Ji's "Expanded Ganlu Characters" and was especially pleased with it. He ordered Dai Xi to write a colophon.
《廣幹祿字》 continues the Ganlu character-book (干祿字) tradition, not the Thousand-Character Classic (千字文).
The heir apparent obtained a copy of Ji's work "Expanded Characters for the Thousand-Character Classic" and was especially pleased, ordering Dai Xi to write a colophon for it.
The heir apparent obtained a copy of Ji's work "Expanded Ganlu Characters" and was especially pleased, ordering Dai Xi to write a colophon for it.
The literal makes the same misidentification of 幹祿字 with the Thousand-Character Classic.
How are the isolated and poor to be extended?
How are the isolated and poor to get ahead?
孤寒者何以伸 asks how the obscure poor are to advance; 伸 is not physical extension.
In the ninth month he sacrificed at the Bright Hall and served as ritual commissioner.
In the ninth month, at the Bright Hall sacrifice, he served as ritual commissioner.
九月祀明堂，為禮儀使 dates the Bright Hall sacrifice and names his office; it does not say he performed the sacrifice himself.

Made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace, he returned home and soon died. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.

Made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace, he returned home and soon died. He was posthumously granted the rank of Grandee of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, with an additional posthumous promotion to Special Advancement.
贈金紫光祿大夫 is a posthumous rank grant, not a territorial enfeoffment.

During the construction of Gaozong's mausoleum, the temporary quarters of the various offices required endless supplies of food and wine. Shen Huan urgently told the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruhe, "The state is in deep mourning, yet officials feast and make merry as usual. How can that be right?"

During the construction of Gaozong's mausoleum, the temporary quarters of the various offices required endless supplies of food and wine. Shen Huan urgently told the pacification commissioner Zheng Ruxie, "The state is in deep mourning, yet officials feast and make merry as usual. How can that be right?"
鄭汝諧 is Zheng Ruxie; Ruhe misreads 諧.
Thereupon those who used the occasion to commit wrongdoing were punished, those who pursued repayment and extortion were pursued for compensation, and expenditures abruptly decreased.
Thereupon those who used the occasion to commit wrongdoing were punished, those who had extorted levies were made to repay them, and expenditures abruptly decreased.
追償率斂者 means those who had extorted levies were made to repay them, not people who pursued repayment.
He was posthumously enfeoffed as direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and given the special posthumous title Duanxian (Upright and Law-abiding).
He was posthumously granted the office of direct academician of the Huawen Pavilion and given the special posthumous title Duanxian (Upright and Law-abiding).
追贈直華文閣 is a posthumous office, not an enfeoffment.
Appointed magistrate of Lizhou, he had not yet taken office when Xue Shusi, pacification commissioner of Jinghu and Hubei, invited him to serve as chief confidential secretary.
Appointed magistrate of Lizhou, he had not yet taken office when Xue Shusi, pacification commissioner of Jinghu, invited him to serve as chief confidential secretary.
宣撫京湖 is the Jinghu theater as one command, not Jinghu and Hubei as two regions.
He was appointed magistrate of Lizhou but had not yet taken up the post when Xue Shusi pacified Jinghu and Hubei and invited him as chief confidential secretary.
He was appointed magistrate of Lizhou but had not yet taken up the post when Xue Shusi, as pacification commissioner of Jinghu, invited him as chief confidential secretary.
宣撫京湖 names Xue Shusi’s office; it does not say he personally pacified Jinghu and Hubei.

He memorialized rewards for Guan as Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously enfeoffed Zhongsheng as Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to two of his descendants.

He memorialized that Guan be appointed Gentleman of Loyal Achievement and registrar of Hanchuan, posthumously granted Zhongsheng the title Gentleman of Martial Cultivation, and gave offices to two of his descendants.
贈仲升修武郎 is a posthumous rank grant, not an enfeoffment.
He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary, but Right Rectifier Zheng Zhao objected and the appointment was shelved.
He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary, but Right Rectifier of Speech Zheng Zhaoxian objected and the appointment was shelved.
鄭昭先 is Zheng Zhaoxian; Zhao drops 先, and 右正言 is Right Rectifier of Speech.
He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary; because right rectifier Zheng Zhao spoke first, the appointment was shelved.
He was promoted to attendant right bureau secretary; because Right Rectifier of Speech Zheng Zhaoxian spoke against it, the appointment was shelved.
以右正言鄭昭先言 is remonstrance by Zheng Zhaoxian, not that Zheng Zhao “spoke first.”
Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, he was made designated drafter of the Baomo Pavilion and magistrate of Chengdu.
Promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review and acting vice minister of the Ministry of Revenue, he was made edict attendant of the Baomo Pavilion and magistrate of Chengdu.
寶謨閣待制 is edict attendant of the Baomo Pavilion, not designated drafter.
He next said, "Take the openness of the Qingli and Yuanyou eras as your model, and the silencing of dissent in the Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning eras as your warning.
He next said, "Take the openness of the Qingli and Yuanyou eras as your model, and the silencing of dissent in the Shaosheng, Chongning, and Daguan eras as your warning.
崇、觀 abbreviates 崇寧 and 大觀 (Chongning and Daguan); Guanning is not an era name here.
He next said: "One should take Qingli and Yuanyou listening to words as the model, and take Shaosheng, Chongning, and Guanning taboo on words as the warning.
